subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group-chat per-user isolation be solved with automatic opt-in group subagents, narrower sender-scoped session/thread extensions, or a generic channel/plugin SDK policy first?
rationale: Current main has partial Feishu primitives, but the requested durable agent lifecycle and per-user skill/config/memory boundaries are product and security choices automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Design Feishu-owned opt-in group subagents
options.body: Approve a Feishu plugin design for per-sender group subagents only after lifecycle TTL, quotas, memory tiers, admin permissions, and message routing proof are specified.

options.title: Extend sender-scoped sessions first
options.body: Keep the current `groupSessionScope` and thread-binding architecture as the default and add only the missing Feishu session/memory seams needed for isolation.

options.title: Require a plugin experiment first
options.body: Keep core lean by asking for an external plugin or ClawHub proof and promote only missing generic SDK hooks if the current plugin API is insufficient.

recommendation.title: Design Feishu-owned opt-in group subagents
recommendation.body: Approve a Feishu plugin design for per-sender group subagents only after lifecycle TTL, quotas, memory tiers, admin permissions, and message routing proof are specified.

likelyOwner.reason: Feishu metadata identifies this handle as the community maintainer, so they are the best available routing owner for the Feishu/plugin-boundary product choice.
